title: The .sufr header is read and written by one module
body:
Three pieces of code know the `.sufr` header layout.

- `SuffixArrayBuilder::open_output` and `finish_output` (`libsufr/src/sufr_builder.rs:865` and `:947`) write it into an `Output` struct (`:971`).
- `SufrFile::read` (`libsufr/src/sufr_file.rs:139-272`) reads it with nine hand-written "8 bytes little-endian as u64" blocks.
- `util::read_text_length` (`libsufr/src/util.rs:95`) reads the version byte and the text length at fixed offsets, separately.

The two native-endian slice casts `slice_int_to_slice_u8` and `vec_to_slice_u8` (`util.rs:123`, `:139`) are unsafe and carry TODOs. `file_access.rs` holds `FileAccess<T>` (`get` at 67, `get_range` at 89, `Iterator::next` at 133) and the positioned `write_at` and `read_exact_at` shim for unix and windows (177-201). The builder has its own `write_all_at` (`sufr_builder.rs:991`).

## Proposal

- `format.rs` holds one `Header` struct, one function that reads it, one that writes it, and named offsets.
- `io.rs` holds `FileAccess<T>`, its iterator, the positioned read/write shim and the two slice casts.
- `SufrFile::read`, the builder's header code and `read_text_length` call `format.rs`. The three copies are deleted.

The `.sufr` bytes do not change. The byte-diff test from the golden-test step must pass unchanged.
close_reason: Landed in 2632038: format.rs (Header, read, write, offsets) and io.rs. Header::read still does not check the version against OUTFILE_VERSION; see sufr-b5ee97.
